UPDATING THE OS FROM A WINDOWS PC USING MIDI-OX

Before starting, close all other audio or MIDI or DAW software, and disconnect all other 
MIDI devices. If necessary, download and install MIDI-OX.

http://www.midiox.com/

Connect the MIDI out of your computer's MIDI interface to Evolver's MIDI in.

1. Run MIDI-OX.
2. From the Options menu, choose "Configure Buffers" and set the Low Level Output Buffers 
   Size to 128 and Num to 1024.
3. Click OK.
4. From the Options menu, choose "MIDI Devices."
5. In the lower left quadrant of the window, select the MIDI port to which the instrument 
   is connected.
	The selected MIDI port appears in the Port Mappings window.
6. Click OK.
7. From the View menu, choose SysEx.
	The SysEx window opens.
8. From the Command Window menu, choose "Load File."
	Browse to and open the SysEx file.
9. From the Command Window menu, choose "Send SysEx."
	The display will count down to 0 as the file is being transferred from the Mac to 
	the instrument. When the transfer is complete, a second, shorter countdown begins as 
	the file is written to memory. Do not turn off the instrument while it is in the 
	process of writing!


************************************* IMPORTANT NOTE *************************************
These are generic instructions for using MIDI-OX. Please refer to the documentation for 
your specific OS update for detailed instructions about what is necessary to update your 
instrument. In some cases, the order in which the operating systems are updated is 
EXTREMELY important. Failure to follow the prescribed procedure could result in an 
instrument that is non-operational and may have to be returned to DSI for repair.

TROUBLESHOOTING

Evolver (desktop model)
If the load fails to start, make sure Evolver is actually receiving MIDI data. (The 
decimal point in the display blinks when receiving MIDI data.) Also, make sure that MIDI 
Receive (Main Row 2, knob 5) is set to "ALL."

Poly Evolver
Poly Evolver Keyboard
Evolver Keyboard
Mopho (desktop model)
Prophet '08 (keyboard and module)
If the load fails to start, make sure the instrument is actually receiving MIDI data. On 
the MIDI Channel page of the Global menu, a dot blinks between "MIDI" and "Channel" when 
MIDI data is received. Also, make sure that MIDI SysEx in the Global menu is set to "On."

Mopho Keyboard (standard and SE)
Tetra
Mopho x4
If the load fails to start, make sure the instrument is actually receiving MIDI data. On the 
MIDI Channel page of the Global menu, a dot blinks between "MIDI" and "Channel" when  MIDI 
data is received. Also, make sure that MIDI SysEx in the Global menu is set to "On." 

Please note: though these instruments are equipped with USB, the operating systems must be 
updated via the 5-pin MIDI jack.

General
Most MIDI interfaces or sound cards with built-in MIDI interfaces will work. However, we 
have received reports that Digidesign/Avid interfaces and Native Instruments Maschine may 
not transmit SysEx correctly for updates. The M-Audio Uno is an inexpensive, reliable, and 
widely available MIDI interface for use when updating our instruments.

If the first countdown stops while the file is being transmitted to the instrument, you 
can safely turn the instrument off and turn it on again. In MIDI-OX, double the Low Level 
Output Buffers "Num" and "Size" values and re-send the SysEx file. If the countdown gets 
closer to zero, then you know your settings are moving in the right direction. If the 
countdown goes further from zero try reducing the "Num" and "Size" settings. You can also 
try doubling or quadrupling the "Size" setting. You may have to adjust the Low Level 
Output Buffers settings several times before finding the right combination.
